title: Prolonged Collagen Peptide Supplementation and Resistance Exercise Training Affects Body Composition in Recreationally Active Men

what_it_measured.text: Abstract: We aimed to determine the effects of long-term collagen peptide (CP) supplementation and resistance exercise training (RET) on body composition, strength, and muscle fiber cross-sectional area (fCSA) in recreationally active men.
In advance, all subjects were informed of theverbally procedure and purpose of this investigation and of possible risks.

dose.text: Fifty-seven young men were randomly and double-blinded divided into a group receiving either collagen peptides (COL, 15 g/day) or a placebo (PLA).

In our younger subjects, in both groups, we found an average protein intake of 1.8 ± 0.5 g/kg-bw/day, which is a sufficient amount to ensure adaptations in an RET regime following already published recommendations [1] and more than double the RDA of 0.8 g/kg-bw/day for the general population.

endpoint.text: Using this line as guidance, only the tissues between aponeuroses, which were not involved in the calculation, were measured.
All measured fibers were averaged for each fiber type, subject, and biopsy sample. 2.10.

The data of the external load of each exercise, the muscle thickness measured via ultrasound in each muscle, and the leg circumferences showed main effects with an increase in each parameter in the whole cohort from pre to post (time: p < 0.05; Table 1).

reported_results.text: COL showed a significant increase in fat-free mass (FFM) compared with the placebo group (p < 0.05).
If the second training set (70% 1RM) was not completed successfully, the training weight was decreased in each exercise, respectively.

No significant differences were found in muscular pain on testing days between groups (DOMS, p > 0.05), and no differences between groups were found in the responses to the RPE scale (p > 0.05) for each exercise within the training period.

The data of the external load of each exercise, the muscle thickness measured via ultrasound in each muscle, and the leg circumferences showed main effects with an increase in each parameter in the whole cohort from pre to post (time: p < 0.05; Table 1).
